title: Local sessions pick up merged settings on their own
why: Oct 22: the owner's Mac ran claude-settings 174 commits behind origin/main, so Mac sessions used old rules and hooks, and nothing showed it.
note: Filed Oct 23 from a prompt the Mac session wrote. Checked at 1842e56: the SessionStart hook tests for a .git folder, but the live copy is a worktree (its .git is a file), so the pull never runs; a pull could not work there anyway (detached HEAD); install.sh reinstalls whatever local main holds; output goes to /dev/null. Advisor ruling, Oct 23 (goal-2 session asked): the old line 'if main is checked out anywhere, skip' would skip on every normal clone, so the hook fast-forwards whichever tree holds main when it is on main with no tracked changes (as merge.py and launch.py already do), else leaves it and logs one line; the pin still follows local main. Windows has the same fault (MINGW branch runs nothing) and this lane fixes it too, per the brief. Open for you: should the pin follow origin/main when local main cannot move (would rewrite decision merge-reinstalls-from-main)? Measured Oct 23: Windows clone on main with 2 untracked stray files and no tracked change, 0 behind; pin at 1842e56 = origin/main. Until it lands, reinstall by hand after each merge on a machine that did not run the merge. Brief: batch 2 of briefs/cleanup-goal-2-oct23.md (full text on c37).
